text:
Micah: Heads up — after yesterday's canary we saw a small but consistent quality cliff when serving a subset of customer traffic with per-layer FP8. Opening a thread to decide the long-term surface: runtime 'switchboard' that applies precision maps per-request vs. baking calibrated profiles per-model-version. Need something that supports per-layer hot-switching, cheap runtime checks, and safe fallbacks.
Anya: +1 on a runtime switchboard, but it must be driven by offline calibration. We can't evaluate full quality online for every request. Suggest a tiny "quality fingerprint" for prompts that we compute offline for eval sets and compare at runtime.
Ryan: Proposal sketch: store a compact quality vector (e.g., 64-byte float32 or quantized) per (model,profile) from the eval harness. At runtime compute same fingerprint on prefix (cheap rolling features), do L2 or cosine compare -> if within threshold, allow aggressive FP8 per-layer maps; otherwise degrade to INT8/4-bit profile. Cheap, stateless, and cacheable per-conversation.
Sophia: Sounds promising. Two caveats: 1) computing fingerprint on every request adds latency — we should cache by conversation_id with TTL and incremental updates, 2) how do we choose thresholds? needs a small calibration job and a continuous regression monitor. Also propose exposing a per-route label `precision_sla: {high,medium,low}` so product teams opt into risk.
Micah: Agree on conversation cache + TTL. For thresholds we can derive operating points from eval curves (precision vs. throughput). Also need a drift detector that flags when a route's fingerprint distribution shifts vs. training/eval distribution.
deploy-bot: Canary fp8-rollout-2026-07: metric "quality_regressions_pct" = 0.72% (+0.60% vs baseline) — flagged by regression-alerts.
Anya: For runtime cost, fingerprint should be sublinear in prefix length: a rolling sketch (e.g., Bloom + average token embedding) or a fixed-window rolling stat. Avoid full-attention re-computation.
Ryan: Example pseudo-config (rough):
```
precision_switch:
  mode: runtime-switchboard
  cache_ttl_s: 120
  profiles:
    - name: fp8-aggressive
      fingerprint_proto: rolling-avg-512
      threshold: 0.11
    - name: int8-safe
      fingerprint_proto: rolling-avg-512
      threshold: 0.30
    - name: 4bit-fallback
      fingerprint_proto: rolling-avg-512
      threshold: 1.0
```
And runtime logic: 
```
fp = fingerprint(prefix)                       # O(1) w.r.t prefix via rolling state
if cache.has(conv_id):                        # use cached profile decision
  profile = cache.get(conv_id)
else:
  delta = compare(fp, profile_signature)
  if delta < profile.threshold:
    profile = fp8-aggressive
  else:
    profile = int8-safe
  cache.set(conv_id, profile, ttl=cache_ttl_s)
apply_precision(profile, per_layer_map)
```
Sophia: Need runtime guardrails: max tokens served under an aggressive profile before re-eval, prod quota on fp8 usage per-customer, and automatic rollback to conservative profile on error spikes. Also log a small sample of outputs for offline re-calibration.
Micah: Action items: 1) Ryan + Anya prototype fingerprint + compare code (pr in 2w), 2) Sophia to draft SLA/ops guardrails and quota ideas, 3) Infra to add lightweight telemetry for drift + per-profile usage. I'll file a short RFC with this sketch. @Sophia @Ryan assign owners? :eyes:
Sophia: I'll take SLA/ops guardrails, will sync with Support on acceptable regression windows.
Ryan: I'll draft the prototype fingerprint and a small microbenchmark for latency/cost.
Anya: I'll own the calibration harness to produce the profile signatures and threshold curves.
Micah: Great — thanks all. Keeping this thread as the huddle for followups.
